symptom: Two items exported a numeric field as 0, and a derived diagnostic agreement was computed from that 0 and published. The underlying quantity had never been authored for either item. Nothing in the export, the diagnostic, or any consumer distinguished the published 0 from a measured 0.
mechanism_as_described: A reader returned 0 when its underlying datum was missing, rather than reporting that it was missing. The 0 then flowed into the export layer and into a derived agreement computed on top of it. An earlier analysis had concluded the fabricated value was never consumed anywhere; that analysis was correct for the classification path it examined and did not cover the export path, so a true statement about one consumer had been read as a statement about all consumers. The scope of the check and the scope of the claim came apart without anyone noticing, because both were phrased as 'it is never consumed'.
detection_path: Replacing the fabricated 0 with an explicit absence marker made a downstream schema check fail loudly, because that consumer required the field to be present. The failure was itself the proof of prior consumption: the absence became visible only when the thing concealing it was removed.
consequence: Two items carried an exported value and a published derived diagnostic computed on a quantity that never existed. The repair also required marking the field nullable downstream, since the honest answer is now representable where before it was not.

extraction_notes.note: The directory reports a sibling change in the same session whose consequence was a previously-masked disagreement becoming visible (a verdict flipping once a certification was withdrawn). That is the repair working as intended, not a second incident.
